indication_weight.population: Adults with obesity (BMI >= 30 kg/m2), or overweight (BMI 27 to <30 kg/m2) with at least one weight-related comorbid condition (dyslipidemia, hypertension, obstructive sleep apnea or CV disease); patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus were excluded. N=2539 randomised 1:1:1:1. Mean baseline weight 104.8 kg, mean BMI 38 kg/m2.
indication_weight.estimand: Intention-to-Treat (ITT) population = all randomised patients. Missing Week 72 body weight was imputed by a hybrid approach using retrieved dropouts from the same treatment group (non-COVID missingness) or all non-missing data assuming missing at random (COVID-19-only missingness). Missingness at Week 72: placebo 21.6%, 5 mg 10.2%, 10 mg 10.5%, 15 mg 9.4%. The label does NOT report an on-treatment estimand for these endpoints; percent changes are LS means from ANCOVA.

between_arm_differences_vs_placebo.note: >=15% and >=20% responder differences for the 5 mg arm are flagged 'e' in the label = 'Not controlled for type I error rate'. The 5 mg >=10% difference is also flagged 'e'. All 10 mg and 15 mg responder differences are flagged 'd' = p<0.001, controlled for type I error rate.

SURMOUNT-2.population: Adults with BMI >= 27 kg/m2 AND type 2 diabetes mellitus, HbA1c 7-10%, on diet/exercise alone or oral agents (DPP-4 inhibitors and GLP-1 RAs excluded; insulin excluded). N=938. Mean baseline weight 100.7 kg, BMI 36.1 kg/m2.

SURMOUNT-3.population: Adults with obesity/overweight (same BMI criteria, no diabetes) who FIRST lost >=5% body weight during a 12-week intensive lifestyle lead-in. 806 enrolled, 579 randomised. Baseline here = Week 0 (after lead-in), mean 101.9 kg.
SURMOUNT-3.note: Change is measured from randomisation (Week 0, after the lifestyle lead-in), NOT from the original baseline. Average lifestyle-induced loss during lead-in was 6.9%.

SURMOUNT-4.population: Adults with obesity/overweight (no diabetes). Open-label tirzepatide 36 weeks, then randomised withdrawal to continue tirzepatide MTD (10 or 15 mg) or switch to placebo for 52 weeks. 670 randomised.
SURMOUNT-4.note: Primary endpoint is % change from Week 36 (randomisation) to Week 88. Mean loss during the 36-week open-label lead-in was 20.9%.

body_composition.source: Look M, Dunn JP, Kushner RF, Cao D, Harris C, Gibble TH, Stefanski A, Griffin R. Body composition changes during weight reduction with tirzepatide in the SURMOUNT-1 study of adults with obesity or overweight. Diabetes Obes Metab. 2025 May;27(5):2720-2729. doi:10.1111/dom.16275 (PMID 39996356; PMCID PMC11965027).
body_composition.notes: The LABEL does not quantify lean vs fat mass - section 12.2 of the Zepbound label states only qualitatively: 'Tirzepatide lowers body weight with greater fat mass loss than lean mass loss.' (PDF p.13). The quantitative figure comes from the DXA substudy of SURMOUNT-1 (n=160 with baseline and Week 72 DXA: pooled tirzepatide n=124, placebo n=36). Verbatim from the published abstract: 'The change in body weight, fat mass and lean mass from baseline to Week 72 was -21.3%, -33.9% and -10.9% with tirzepatide and -5.3%, -8.2% and -2.6% with placebo, respectively (p < 0.001 for all comparisons). Of the body weight lost, approximately 75% was fat mass and 25% was lean mass for both tirzepatide and placebo.' NOTE: this 25% lean-mass fraction is the same for tirzepatide and placebo, i.e. the drug did not change the COMPOSITION of the weight lost in this substudy. Also note the substudy population (mean weight 102.5 kg, BMI 38.0) is not identical to the full SURMOUNT-1 population.

tirzepatide.notes: Zepbound percent-weight-change values are LS means from ANCOVA on the ITT population with hybrid imputation; they are NOT on-treatment/observed-case values. Because 21.6% of placebo patients had missing Week 72 weight versus ~10% on tirzepatide, the ITT-based placebo value (-3.1%) already incorporates retrieved-dropout imputation; an observed-case or on-treatment analysis would give different numbers, which the label does not provide. SURMOUNT-1 enrolled almost no patients with type 2 diabetes (excluded), so these numbers must not be quoted as expected weight loss in a patient with diabetes - use SURMOUNT-2 (-14.7% at 15 mg) for that population. Mounjaro (the diabetes brand) reports NO percent weight change and no weight-loss responder rates anywhere in its label.

body_composition.notes: NOT VERIFIED. The Wegovy label states only qualitatively, in section 12.2 Pharmacodynamics (PDF p.21 of the 02/2026 accessdata label): 'Semaglutide lowers body weight with greater fat mass loss than lean mass loss.' No percentage or proportion is given anywhere in the label. The STEP 1 DXA body-composition analysis that is usually cited exists as a conference abstract (J Endocr Soc 2021;5(Suppl 1):A16-A17) and as a review summary (O'Neil PM, Rubino DM. Postgrad Med. 2022;134(sup1):28-36. doi:10.1080/00325481.2022.2150006), which states only that 'reductions in total fat mass were greater with semaglutide versus placebo'. I could not retrieve a full peer-reviewed primary publication reporting the lean-mass percentage for semaglutide 2.4 mg in STEP 1, so this field is left null rather than filled from memory or a secondary summary.

semaglutide_2_4.notes: The 2.4 mg numbers are identical in the 02/2026 FDA-distributed PDF and the newer 2026-06-30 SPL. Be careful with study numbering: the Wegovy label calls STEP 1 'Study 2', STEP 2 'Study 3', STEP 3 'Study 4', STEP 4 'Study 5', and SELECT 'Study 1'. The >=20% responder difference for STEP 1 is flagged in the label as 'Not included in the pre-specified hierarchical testing' - it is descriptive. Wegovy is now approved in three forms (2.4 mg injection, 7.2 mg injection, 25 mg oral tablet); do not mix their numbers.

liraglutide_3_0.notes: Important asymmetry: Saxenda's label reports ONLY >=5% and >=10% responder rates. There is no >=15% or >=20% figure anywhere in the label - do not infer them. The 56-week values are the primary endpoint; the 160-week values are descriptive percentages of patients 'known to lose >=5%', not LS means. Also note that in the 56-week trials all-cause discontinuation of study drug was LOWER with SAXENDA (27%) than with placebo (35%), and in the 160-week trial 47% vs 55%.

dulaglutide.notes: Trulicity is included in this dataset mainly as the active comparator in SURPASS-CVOT and because it is a GLP-1 RA, but it has NO weight-management indication and its weight effects (-2 to -4.6 kg) are much smaller than the dedicated weight-management agents. Do not present Trulicity weight numbers as 'weight loss efficacy' alongside Zepbound/Wegovy numbers - the populations (type 2 diabetes), endpoints (HbA1c primary) and durations differ, and percent weight change is not reported at all.

cross_trial_caveat: Numbers from different trials must never be compared head-to-head. Each label value comes from a distinct randomised population with different inclusion criteria (with vs without type 2 diabetes, BMI thresholds, baseline weight and HbA1c), different background therapy and lifestyle intervention, different run-in or withdrawal designs, different treatment durations and endpoint weeks, and different statistical estimands and missing-data imputation rules (Zepbound/SURMOUNT used ITT with hybrid retrieved-dropout imputation and had ~22% missing Week 72 weight in the placebo arm; Wegovy/STEP used ITT with RD-MI; Saxenda used all-available on-treatment data with multiple imputation or weighted regression; Mounjaro/Ozempic/Trulicity report glycaemic endpoints in a modified-ITT population with multiple imputation and rescue-medication rules, and report body weight only in kilograms). Trial-level differences in adherence, discontinuation and dose escalation (e.g. Zepbound 5 mg is a fixed dose while SURMOUNT-3/4 used a maximum tolerated dose of 10 or 15 mg) alone can move the apparent effect size by several percentage points. Only randomised head-to-head trials (e.g. SURPASS-2, tirzepatide vs semaglutide 1 mg) support direct comparisons, and even those are limited to the specific doses and populations studied. For a patient-facing app, the correct framing is an expected range for the specific drug, dose, population and time point, always presented together with the placebo arm, rather than a single 'best' number.
